manifestations.description: remained unconscious for the greater part of the next nine or ten days
partial deafness in the left ear
tinnitus in both ears (somewhat worse in the left ear)
difficulty in maintaining his balance particularly after he stoops to pick something up / disturbance in equilibrium
episodes of 'loss of focus' when he reads for more than half an hour
a numb sensation over the left upper face and cheek
some pain in the lower part of the back
reduced memory and concentration; inclined to forget small matters and must concentrate harder at work
increased tendency to be more irritable (tendency managed so far)
reduced capacity for golf / tires more quickly and can play only 18 holes instead of 36

treatments_received: operation to the left ear (blood clots removed from the middle ear; ear-drum repaired)
audiograms (ear, nose and throat clinic at Sai Ying Poon)
out-patient attendances at Queen Mary Hospital for many months
consultations (Dr. Singh; Dr. Heffernan); change of glasses

losses.description: Partial deafness in the left ear and tinnitus in both ears (worse in the left ear).
Fractures of the skull (including left parietal, left petrous and base of skull) and other injuries to head, neck, spine and left side of the body.
Difficulty in maintaining balance, occasional dizziness and reduced stamina for exertion (e.g. can now play only 18 holes of golf instead of 36).
Reduced memory and concentration; must concentrate harder to achieve prior level of work; forgets small matters.
Increased tendency to irritability (managed so far).

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Reduced ability to play long games of golf and tires more quickly.
